# Problem 1
```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")

dim(ny_noaa)
str(ny_noaa)
colSums(is.na(ny_noaa))
```

The NY NOAA dataset has 2,595,176 rows and 7 columns. It is a tibble containing daily weather records from different stations. The main variables include station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and maximum and minimum temperatures. There are many missing values, especially for tmax and tmin, which each have over 1.1 million missing values. Other weather variables also have missing values, but ID and date do not.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

noaa_clean <- ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )

sort(table(noaa_clean$snow), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
```

The most common snowfall value is 0 mm, with 2,008,508 observations, because most days have no snow. The next most common values are 25 mm and 13 mm, likely because snowfall measurements were converted from inches to metric units.


```{r}
library(ggplot2)

jan_jul <- noaa_clean |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 7, !is.na(tmax)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c(1, 7),
                   labels = c("January", "July"))
  )

ggplot(jan_jul, aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~month) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1985, 1995, 2005)) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

January temperatures are much lower and vary more across years, while July temperatures are more consistent, mostly around 25–30°C. There is no clear overall trend over time. There are a few outliers, especially some unusually low temperatures in July.



```{r}
library(ggridges)
library(patchwork)

snow_data <- noaa_clean |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100)

snow_plot <- ggplot(snow_data, aes(x = snow, y = factor(year))) +
  geom_density_ridges(fill = "grey75", scale = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

temp_data <- noaa_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin))

temp_plot <- ggplot(temp_data, aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex(bins = 35) +
  labs(
    title = "Max vs Min Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

temp_plot + snow_plot
```

Snowfall amounts are mostly low, and the distributions look similar across years with no clear trend. There is a clear positive relationship between tmin and tmax, with a few unusual values outside the main pattern.


# Problem 2
```{r}
nhanes_covar <- read.csv("data/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4)
nhanes_accel <- read.csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv")
```

```{r}
library(tidyr)

nhanes_covar_clean <- nhanes_covar |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2),
                 labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    education = factor(education, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                       labels = c("Less than high school",
                                  "High school equivalent",
                                  "More than high school"))
  )

nhanes_tidy <- nhanes_accel |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    values_to = "MIMS"
  ) |>
  mutate(minute = as.integer(sub("min", "", minute))) |>
  inner_join(nhanes_covar_clean, by = "SEQN")
```

```{r}
education_table <- nhanes_covar_clean |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  )

knitr::kable(education_table)
```

```{r}
ggplot(nhanes_covar_clean, aes(x = sex, y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  labs(
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age"
  )
```

The more than high school group has the most participants, with 56 men and 59 women. The high school equivalent group has more men than women. For age distributions, men and women have similar median ages in the less than high school group. Women have a higher median age in the high school equivalent group, while both sexes are generally younger in the more than high school group.



```{r}
total_activity <- nhanes_tidy |>
  group_by(SEQN, age, sex, education) |>
  summarize(total_MIMS = sum(MIMS), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(total_activity, aes(x = age, y = total_MIMS)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sex)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(linetype = sex), method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "Total Activity (MIMS)",
    shape = "Sex",
    linetype = "Sex"
  )
```
  

Total activity generally decreases with age across all three education groups. Women tend to have higher total activity than men in the high school equivalent and more than high school groups. In the less than high school group, the trends for men and women are fairly similar.


```{r}
activity_time <- nhanes_tidy |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute) |>
  summarize(
    mean_MIMS = mean(MIMS, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(activity_time,
       aes(x = (minute - 1) / 60, y = mean_MIMS, color = sex)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "grey60")) +
  labs(
    x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Average Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  )
```

Activity is lowest during the early morning and increases during the day, then decreases again at night. Women generally have higher activity levels than men, especially in the more than high school group. The overall daily activity patterns are similar across the three education groups.



# Problem 3

```{r}
jan_2020 <- read.csv("data/Jan 2020 Citi.csv")
jul_2020 <- read.csv("data/July 2020 Citi.csv")
jan_2024 <- read.csv("data/Jan 2024 Citi.csv")
jul_2024 <- read.csv("data/July 2024 Citi.csv")
```

```{r}
citi_bike <- bind_rows(
  mutate(jan_2020, year = 2020, month = "January"),
  mutate(jul_2020, year = 2020, month = "July"),
  mutate(jan_2024, year = 2024, month = "January"),
  mutate(jul_2024, year = 2024, month = "July")
) |>
  mutate(
    weekdays = factor(weekdays,
                      levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
                                 "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"))
  )
```

The cleaned Citi Bike dataset has 99,485 rows and 9 columns, with each row representing one ride. It includes ride ID, bike type, weekday, ride duration, starting and ending stations, membership status, year, and month. Some station names are missing, but these rides are kept in the dataset.


```{r}
ride_table <- citi_bike |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n
  )

knitr::kable(ride_table)
```

Members took more rides than casual riders in every month. July had more rides than January in both years, and 2024 had more rides than 2020. July 2024 had the most rides, with 36,262 member rides and 10,894 casual rides in the dataset.


```{r}
top_stations <- citi_bike |>
filter(year == 2024, month == "July",
       !is.na(start_station_name))|>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(5)

knitr::kable(top_stations)
```


```{r}
ride_duration <- citi_bike |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(ride_duration, aes(x = weekdays, y = median_duration)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(year ~ month) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
                              "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")) +
  labs(
    x = "Day of Week",
    y = "Median Ride Duration (minutes)"
  )
```

Median ride duration is generally longer in July than in January. Weekend rides also tend to be longer than weekday rides, especially in July. Ride durations in 2020 are generally longer than in 2024, with the biggest difference in July.
  
```{r}
citi_2024 <- citi_bike |>
  filter(year == 2024)

ggplot(citi_2024, aes(x = member_casual, y = duration)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(month ~ rideable_type) +
  labs(
    x = "Membership Status",
    y = "Ride Duration (minutes)"
  )
```
  
Casual riders generally have longer rides than members in both months. Ride durations are also longer in July than in January. Classic bikes tend to have longer rides for casual riders, while electric bikes have slightly longer rides for members. There are many outliers with much longer ride durations.
